name: Organic Chemistry
description: The study of the structure, properties, reactions, and synthesis of carbon-based compounds.

name: Inorganic Chemistry
description: The study of the structure, properties, and reactions of elements and compounds that are not carbon-organic, spanning metals, minerals, and coordination complexes.

name: Physical Chemistry
description: The branch applying physics concepts to explain chemical systems, including thermodynamics, kinetics, and quantum behavior.

name: Analytical Chemistry
description: The science of separating, identifying, and quantifying the chemical components of matter.

name: Biochemistry
description: The study of chemical processes and molecules within and relating to living organisms.

name: Theoretical Chemistry
description: The development of mathematical and computational models to describe chemical structure, bonding, and reactivity.

name: Polymer Chemistry
description: The study of the synthesis, structure, and properties of macromolecules and polymers.

name: Nuclear Chemistry
description: The study of radioactive elements, nuclear transformations, and the chemical effects of radiation.

name: Medicinal Chemistry
description: The chemistry discipline devoted to the design, synthesis, and optimization of pharmaceutical agents.

name: Food Chemistry
description: The study of the chemical composition, reactions, and transformations of food during processing and storage.

name: Environmental Chemistry
description: The study of chemical phenomena in natural environments and the fate of pollutants in air, water, and soil.

name: Materials Chemistry
description: The chemistry-driven design, synthesis, and understanding of solid and functional materials.

name: Alchemy
description: The historical proto-scientific practice combining metallurgy, mysticism, and early chemistry in pursuit of metal transmutation and an elixir of life.

name: Chinese Alchemy
description: The Taoist-influenced Chinese proto-chemical tradition seeking elixirs of immortality, which contributed to early gunpowder and pharmaceutical chemistry.

name: Organic Reaction Mechanisms
description: The study of the step-by-step pathways by which organic reactions proceed at the molecular level.

name: Stereochemistry
description: The study of the three-dimensional spatial arrangement of atoms in molecules and its effect on reactivity.

name: Organic Synthesis
description: The construction of organic compounds through planned sequences of chemical reactions.

name: Total Synthesis
description: The complete laboratory construction of complex natural products from simple starting materials.

name: Retrosynthetic Analysis
description: A problem-solving strategy that works backward from a target molecule to identify simpler precursor structures.

name: Asymmetric Synthesis
description: The selective preparation of one enantiomer or diastereomer of a chiral molecule.

name: Organocatalysis
description: The acceleration of reactions using small organic molecules as catalysts instead of metals or enzymes.

name: Heterocyclic Chemistry
description: The chemistry of ring compounds containing heteroatoms such as nitrogen, oxygen, or sulfur.

name: Natural Product Chemistry
description: The isolation, characterization, and synthesis of chemical compounds produced by living organisms.

name: Carbohydrate Chemistry
description: The study of the structure, synthesis, and reactions of sugars and polysaccharides.

name: Organic Photochemistry
description: The study of light-induced chemical reactions of organic molecules.

name: Physical Organic Chemistry
description: The quantitative study of the relationship between organic molecular structure and reactivity using physical principles.

name: Supramolecular Chemistry
description: The chemistry of non-covalent interactions and the assemblies of multiple molecules into larger structures.

name: Coordination Chemistry
description: The study of compounds in which metal centers are bound to surrounding ligands.

name: Crystal Field Theory
description: A model describing the electronic structure and colors of transition-metal complexes via ligand-induced splitting of d-orbitals.

name: Ligand Field Theory
description: An extension of crystal field theory incorporating covalent metal-ligand bonding into molecular orbital descriptions.

name: Organometallic Chemistry
description: The study of compounds containing direct metal-carbon bonds.

name: Bioinorganic Chemistry
description: The study of the roles of metals and metalloenzymes in biological systems.

name: Solid State Chemistry
description: The synthesis, structure, and properties of solid-phase materials and their phase behavior.

name: Main Group Chemistry
description: The chemistry of the s- and p-block elements of the periodic table.

name: Transition Metal Chemistry
description: The chemistry of the d-block elements and their characteristic variable oxidation states and complexes.

name: Lanthanide and Actinide Chemistry
description: The chemistry of the rare-earth lanthanide and radioactive actinide elements.

name: Metal Cluster Chemistry
description: The study of compounds in which multiple metal atoms are directly bonded into clusters.

name: Chemical Thermodynamics
description: The study of energy, entropy, and spontaneity in chemical reactions and phase changes.

name: Thermochemistry
description: The measurement and interpretation of heat changes accompanying chemical processes.

name: Chemical Equilibrium
description: The state of a reversible reaction in which forward and reverse rates balance and concentrations stabilize.

name: Solution Thermodynamics
description: The thermodynamics of mixing, solvation, and non-ideal behavior in solutions.

name: Chemical Kinetics
description: The study of reaction rates, rate laws, and the mechanisms controlling them.

name: Reaction Dynamics
description: The detailed study of how energy and molecular collisions determine reaction pathways.

name: Catalysis
description: The acceleration of chemical reactions by substances that are not consumed in the process.

name: Homogeneous Catalysis
description: Catalysis in which the catalyst and reactants share a single phase, typically solution.

name: Heterogeneous Catalysis
description: Catalysis occurring at the surface of a solid catalyst in a different phase from the reactants.

name: Photocatalysis
description: Catalysis driven by light-absorbing materials that generate reactive species at surfaces.

name: Electrochemistry
description: The study of the interconversion of chemical and electrical energy at electrodes and in ionic conductors.

name: Battery Chemistry
description: The chemistry of charge storage, electrode materials, and electrolytes in electrochemical cells.

name: Statistical Mechanics
description: The bridge from microscopic molecular behavior to macroscopic thermodynamic properties via ensemble averages.

name: Surface Chemistry
description: The study of physical and chemical phenomena at the interfaces of phases, including adsorption.

name: Colloid and Interface Chemistry
description: The study of dispersed systems such as emulsions, foams, and suspensions with large interfacial area.

name: Photochemistry
description: The study of chemical reactions initiated or mediated by the absorption of light.

name: Quantum Chemistry
description: The application of quantum mechanics to molecular structure, bonding, and electronic spectra.

name: Molecular Orbital Theory
description: A quantum model describing bonding in terms of delocalized molecular orbitals formed from atomic orbitals.

name: Valence Bond Theory
description: A quantum model describing bonding in terms of localized overlapping atomic orbitals and resonance.

name: Computational Chemistry
description: The use of computer simulation and numerical methods to model chemical systems and predict properties.

name: Ab Initio Methods
description: Quantum chemical calculations derived from first principles without empirical parameters.

name: Density Functional Theory
description: A widely used quantum method computing electronic structure from the electron density distribution.

name: Semiempirical Methods
description: Approximate quantum calculations that incorporate experimental parameters to reduce computational cost.

name: Molecular Mechanics
description: Classical force-field models of molecular geometry and energy that ignore electronic motion.

name: Molecular Dynamics
description: Simulation of the time evolution of molecular systems by integrating classical equations of motion.

name: Monte Carlo Simulation
description: Stochastic sampling methods for computing thermodynamic averages of molecular systems.

name: Cheminformatics
description: The use of computational and information techniques to store, retrieve, and analyze chemical data.

name: Quantitative Structure-Activity Relationship
description: Statistical models relating molecular structure descriptors to biological or chemical activity.

name: Mathematical Chemistry
description: The application of mathematics, especially graph theory, to chemical structure and properties.

name: Chemical Graph Theory
description: The representation of molecules as graphs to study topology, isomerism, and molecular descriptors.

name: Polymer Synthesis
description: The methods by which monomers are linked into high-molecular-weight polymer chains.

name: Step-Growth Polymerization
description: Polymerization in which multifunctional monomers react stepwise, as in polyesters and polyamides.

name: Chain-Growth Polymerization
description: Polymerization that proceeds by reactive-center propagation along a growing chain.

name: Radical Polymerization
description: Chain-growth polymerization propagated by free-radical intermediates.

name: Ionic Polymerization
description: Chain-growth polymerization propagated by cationic or anionic active centers.

name: Coordination Polymerization
description: Polymerization mediated by transition-metal catalysts that control stereochemistry, as in Ziegler-Natta catalysis.

name: Ring-Opening Polymerization
description: Polymerization initiated by opening cyclic monomers such as lactones and epoxides.

name: Polymer Characterization
description: The measurement of molecular weight, structure, and thermal and mechanical properties of polymers.

name: Polymer Physics
description: The physical theory of polymer conformations, elasticity, and viscoelasticity.

name: Biopolymers
description: Naturally occurring macromolecules such as proteins, nucleic acids, and polysaccharides.

name: Conductive Polymers
description: Organic polymers that conduct electricity through conjugated backbones and doping.

name: Polymer Rheology
description: The study of the flow and deformation behavior of polymer melts and solutions.

name: Radiochemistry
description: The chemistry of radioactive isotopes, their preparation, separation, and measurement.

name: Radiation Chemistry
description: The study of chemical effects produced by ionizing radiation on matter.

name: Isotope Chemistry
description: The study of the chemical behavior and separation of isotopes of the elements.

name: Actinide Chemistry
description: The chemistry of the radioactive actinide series, including uranium, plutonium, and transuranics.

name: Radioanalytical Chemistry
description: Analytical techniques using radioactivity and nuclear properties to measure trace species.

name: Nuclear Forensics
description: The analysis of nuclear and radioactive materials to determine their origin, history, and intended use.

name: Qualitative Analysis
description: The identification of which chemical species are present in a sample.

name: Quantitative Analysis
description: The determination of the amount or concentration of chemical species in a sample.

name: Gravimetric Analysis
description: Quantification by measuring the mass of a purified analyte or its precipitate.

name: Titrimetry
description: Volumetric quantification by reacting an analyte with a reagent of known concentration to an endpoint.

name: Instrumental Analysis
description: Analysis performed with electronic instruments measuring physical properties of analytes.

name: Spectroscopy
description: The measurement of the interaction of electromagnetic radiation with matter to identify and quantify species.

name: Atomic Spectroscopy
description: Spectroscopic techniques that analyze free atoms in the gas phase.

name: Atomic Absorption Spectroscopy
description: Quantification of elements by measuring light absorbed by ground-state atoms.

name: Atomic Emission Spectroscopy
description: Quantification of elements by measuring light emitted from excited atoms in a plasma or flame.

name: Molecular Spectroscopy
description: Spectroscopic study of molecules through their rotational, vibrational, and electronic transitions.

name: UV-Visible Spectroscopy
description: Absorption spectroscopy in the ultraviolet-visible region probing electronic transitions.

name: Infrared Spectroscopy
description: Absorption spectroscopy in the infrared region probing molecular vibrations and functional groups.

name: Raman Spectroscopy
description: Inelastic light scattering spectroscopy probing vibrational modes complementary to infrared absorption.

name: Fluorescence Spectroscopy
description: Emission spectroscopy of light released as excited molecules relax, used for sensitive detection.

name: NMR Spectroscopy
description: Nuclear magnetic resonance spectroscopy resolving molecular structure via nuclear spin transitions in magnetic fields.

name: Mass Spectrometry
description: The measurement of the mass-to-charge ratios of ionized molecules for identification and quantification.

name: Gas Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry
description: Hyphenated separation and identification of volatile compounds by gas chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry.

name: Liquid Chromatography-Mass Spectrometry
description: Separation and identification of non-volatile and polar analytes by liquid chromatography coupled to mass spectrometry.

name: Tandem Mass Spectrometry
description: Multiple-stage mass spectrometry in which selected ions are fragmented for structural elucidation.

name: Chromatography
description: Separation of mixtures by differential partitioning between a stationary and a mobile phase.

name: Gas Chromatography
description: Separation of volatile compounds in a gaseous mobile phase through a coated capillary column.

name: Liquid Chromatography
description: Separation of analytes in a liquid mobile phase passed through a packed column.

name: High-Performance Liquid Chromatography
description: High-pressure liquid chromatography providing rapid, high-resolution separation of complex mixtures.

name: Thin-Layer Chromatography
description: Planar chromatography on a coated plate used for rapid qualitative screening.

name: Ion Chromatography
description: Separation and quantification of ions using ion-exchange stationary phases and conductivity detection.

name: Size-Exclusion Chromatography
description: Separation of macromolecules by molecular size through a porous gel matrix.

name: Electroanalytical Methods
description: Analytical techniques based on the electrical response of analyte solutions at electrodes.

name: Potentiometry
description: Measurement of electrode potential to determine analyte concentration, as in pH electrodes.

name: Voltammetry
description: Measurement of current as a function of applied potential for trace analysis of electroactive species.

name: Coulometry
description: Quantification by measuring the total charge passed during complete electrolysis of an analyte.

name: Thermal Analysis
description: Measurement of material properties as a function of temperature.

name: Differential Scanning Calorimetry
description: Measurement of heat flow into a sample to characterize phase transitions and thermal stability.

name: Thermogravimetric Analysis
description: Measurement of mass change with temperature to study decomposition and volatilization.

name: Separation Science
description: The systematic study and development of methods to resolve mixtures into pure components.

name: Sample Preparation
description: Techniques for extracting, concentrating, and cleaning samples before instrumental analysis.

name: Chemometrics
description: The application of statistical and mathematical methods to chemical measurement and data.

name: Bioanalytical Chemistry
description: Analytical methods for measuring molecules in biological matrices such as blood and tissue.

name: Drug Design
description: The rational design of new therapeutic molecules based on biological target structure.

name: Computer-Aided Drug Design
description: Computational methods for discovering and optimizing drug candidates, including docking and virtual screening.

name: Pharmacokinetics
description: The quantitative study of drug absorption, distribution, metabolism, and excretion over time.

name: Drug Metabolism
description: The biochemical transformation of drugs in the body, largely by liver enzymes.

name: Combinatorial Chemistry
description: The rapid synthesis of large libraries of related compounds for screening.

name: Peptide Therapeutics
description: The design and chemistry of peptide-based drugs and their stabilization for clinical use.

name: Flavor Chemistry
description: The study of the volatile and non-volatile compounds responsible for food aroma and taste.

name: Food Analysis
description: Analytical determination of nutrients, contaminants, and additives in food products.

name: Food Additives
description: Chemical substances added to foods to preserve, color, sweeten, or stabilize them.

name: Nutraceuticals
description: Food-derived compounds with physiological or medicinal benefits beyond basic nutrition.

name: Food Biochemistry
description: The biochemical reactions of enzymes and nutrients during food production and storage.

name: Aquatic Chemistry
description: The chemistry of natural waters, including speciation, redox, and acid-base equilibria.

name: Green Chemistry
description: The design of chemical products and processes that reduce or eliminate hazardous substances.

name: Environmental Analysis
description: Analytical measurement of pollutants and trace chemicals in environmental media.

name: Nanochemistry
description: The chemical synthesis and study of materials at the nanoscale.

name: Crystal Engineering
description: The design of crystalline solids with desired properties by controlling intermolecular interactions.

name: Metal-Organic Frameworks
description: Porous crystalline materials built from metal nodes and organic linkers, used for storage and separation.

name: Zeolite Chemistry
description: The chemistry of microporous aluminosilicate minerals used as catalysts and adsorbents.
